cards.english: Have a good flight!
We took out the trash.
The child wants ice cream.
I reached the station.
They arrived by train.
I need your help.
cards.existing: Many verbs require dative without 'to': `помогать` (help), `звонить` (phone), `советовать` (advise), `мешать` (disturb). `Помогаю маме` (I help mom).

cards.english: Hi, Oleg! How are things?
Hi, Natasha! How are things?
The children came from school.
Grandfather turned seventy.
The students bought bread yesterday.
She came out of the store.
I need to call my parents.
The friends were reading a book yesterday.
The bus pulled up to the stop.
Friends liked our new house.
cards.existing: Person who likes goes dative (мне, тебе, ему, ей, нам, вам, им). The verb agrees with what's liked, not the liker: `нравится` (sg) vs `нравятся` (pl).

cards.english: Children know everything about dinosaurs.
We moved the meeting to tomorrow.
He watches the news every evening.
cards.existing: `Никогда не` (Nikogda ne) – Russian doubles up on negatives. `Я никогда не был там` (I never not have-been there). Don't drop the `не`; it's required.

cards.english: The food is delicious at this restaurant.
cards.existing: Hard consonant before ending? Likely `-ут/-ат`. Soft (vowel-like)? Likely `-ют/-ят`. The spelling rule follows from the stem's consonant.

cards.english: We are going to the park for a walk.
cards.existing: Walking vs vehicle: `идти (idti)/ходить` for on foot, `ехать/ездить` for any vehicle. Russian distinguishes how you move, English doesn't.

cards.target: Она нашла потерянную кошку во дворе.
cards.english: She found the lost cat in the yard.

cards.target: Брат плавал в бассейне на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: Brother swam in the pool last week.

cards.target: Мы переехали в новую квартиру в прошлом месяце.
cards.english: We moved to a new apartment last month.

cards.target: Дедушка убирал квартиру на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: Grandfather cleaned the apartment last week.
The plane took off on time.
I visited all the stores.
The doctor prescribed medicine to the patient.
The teacher explained the rule to the students.
He delivered gifts to all friends.
cards.existing: `Весь (Ves)/вся/всё/все` covers 'all', 'the whole', 'everyone', 'everything' depending on form. Context + ending tells you which.

cards.target: Программист ездит на работу каждый день.
cards.english: The programmer commutes to work every day.
Someone from the office called you.
Yesterday I visited an art exhibition.
Several students were late for the lecture.
The salesman washes dishes at home now.
How do you say this word in Russian?
The scent of flowers filled the entire room.
A piece of cake remained on the plate.
Children are not allowed to watch this movie.
The pages of the book have yellowed with time.

cards.target: Рад познакомиться с вами наконец лично.
cards.english: I'm pleased to finally meet you in person.
cards.existing: Instrumental case marks the tool, means, or accompaniment: `пишу карандашом` (write with pencil), `еду с другом` (go with a friend). Endings: -ом/-ем (m/n), -ой/-ей (f), -ью (f soft), -ами/-ями (pl).

cards.target: Нам удалось купить билеты на концерт.
cards.english: We managed to buy tickets for the concert.
Half past four.
cards.existing: Russian doesn't use 'to be' in the present: `Я студент` (Ya student) literally = 'I student' = 'I am a student'. The verb is implied. Adding `есть` would be old-fashioned.

cards.english: Quarter to seven.
Quarter past five.
cards.existing: When you'd say 'is/are' in English, Russian usually says nothing. `Это дом` (Eto dom) = 'this house' = 'this is a house'. The pause does the work.
